answer: A network can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to forge a stake-bonded reputation over time: a new agent must complete a long history of verified useful work before earning weight, so spinning up a thousand cheap identities costs as much as a thousand honest ones. Like a juniper that grows slowly and a nebula that only condenses under gravity, trust accrues gradually and cannot be faked in bulk — an attacker must pay the same time-and-stake cost per identity as any legitimate participant.
